# mulib-img-core

<!-- Generated by tools/media_inventory.py; edit CONTRACTS or section-7 scope, then --write-docs. -->

**Area:** Image  
**Implementation:** C11 `static inline`; no implementation switch or external ABI export  
**Status:** bounded review candidate; **not safe On1x admitted**

## Purpose and limits

Float RGBA strided image view and pixel math.

get/put are unchecked internal primitives; validate and bound indices first. Linear light, straight alpha by convention.

Current header refinement: get/put are unchecked internal primitives; validate and bound indices first.

Retain existing upstream functionality and platform providers; this header is not a replacement for a complete media/editor/rendering stack.

## Units, ownership and capacities

get/put are unchecked: first validate the view and ensure x<width, y<height. clamp_index requires a nonzero n. luma/lerp operate on values, not on a color-managed display image. Validators cannot prove a caller-supplied backing allocation.

Images are linear-light, straight RGBA float views. Width/height are pixels; stride and capacity count float elements, not bytes. A row needs width*4 floats and the live extent is (height-1)*stride+width*4. Keep all backing storage alive. Supply finite coordinates and parameters. HDR RGB is not implicitly display-referred; transparent filtering needs explicit premultiplication/unpremultiplication. Distinct pointers alone do not prove nonoverlap.

Capacities describe live backing storage supplied by the caller, not merely numeric metadata. Check return values before using outputs. A false result is not a universal no-mutation guarantee; low-level value helpers and bool miss/error results require the documented preconditions. Bound untrusted counts and work before calling.

## Current callable surface

Signatures extracted from this header; dependency types and complete checks are in [the source](../kernels/mulib-img-core.h). Helpers listed here are not automatically safe foreign imports.

```c
static inline bool mulib_img_memory_span(const void *p,size_t n,size_t element,size_t *bytes);
static inline bool mulib_img_memory_disjoint(const void *a,size_t an,size_t ae,const void *b,size_t bn,size_t be);
static inline bool mulib_img_span(mulib_img_view v,size_t *elements);
static inline bool mulib_img_valid(mulib_img_view v);
static inline bool mulib_img_disjoint(mulib_img_view a,mulib_img_view b);
static inline bool mulib_img_pointwise_alias(mulib_img_view a,mulib_img_view b);
static inline bool mulib_img_disjoint_array(mulib_img_view v,const void *p,size_t n,size_t element);
static inline mulib_img_rgba mulib_img_get(mulib_img_view v,size_t x,size_t y);
static inline void mulib_img_put(mulib_img_view v,size_t x,size_t y,mulib_img_rgba c);
static inline bool mulib_img_same(mulib_img_view a,mulib_img_view b);
static inline float mulib_img_luma(mulib_img_rgba a);
static inline mulib_img_rgba mulib_img_lerp(mulib_img_rgba a,mulib_img_rgba b,float t);
static inline size_t mulib_img_clamp_index(int64_t x,size_t n);
```

## Additional source contracts

- stride and capacity are in float elements, NOT bytes. The caller must provide an actual accessible allocation matching capacity; validation cannot prove it.
- Conservative enclosing byte ranges, including padding. Invalid spans fail.
- Pointwise operations allow exactly the same mapping, but not shifted aliases.
- n must be positive for image access; n==0 returns 0, never SIZE_MAX.

## Validation and integration

The [shared CPU example](../examples/media-pipeline.c) illustrates a small image/audio/timebase slice; it does **not** exercise every API in this header. The [integration oracles](../tests/media-integration-test.c) and [parser boundary probes](../tests/media-parser-boundary-test.c) are representative regressions, not exhaustive coverage.

```sh
python3 tools/check_media.py
```

The runner checks the 193 original kernels plus the shared PCM helper, isolated and in aggregate C11 builds with GCC/Clang, including canonical-header composition, separate-TU wrappers, an expected missing-static-inline-export link failure, a no-`__int128` path, and ASan/UBSan regressions. It does not validate native GPU/codec/audio execution, real-world compatibility, C++ or On1x ownership/admission. Explicit foreign wrappers, independent safety review and platform integration are still required.
